note: Hand-curated. Every entry needs a source URL from a news outlet before it ships — scripts/suggest_openings.py surfaces candidates and the Brief's archive (btownbrief/archive stories.json openClose tags) is the deep well; a human verifies and adds them here. Dates we could not pin to a day carry a 'reported' label.

entries.name: Ray's Seafood Market & Restaurant
entries.story: The family business that started as a wholesale seafood provider 74 years ago announced it will close, giving no reason for the decision — one last month for a final basket of fried clams.

entries.name: Mirabelles at the Kitchen Table spots ('Belles on the River)
entries.dateLabel: reopenings targeted by end of September 2026
entries.story: Mirabelles is taking over both former Kitchen Table locations — the Richmond restaurant will likely become 'Belles on the River, serving casual dinners plus weekend brunch with the popovers along for the ride.

entries.name: Sneakeasy (at Sneakers Bistro)
entries.story: The 1980 breakfast-and-lunch staple is going nighttime with an upstairs cocktail lounge — a clarified Bloody Mary martini, bar bites that nod to Belizean fry jacks, and thrifted-decor charm. Daytime service stays exactly as it was.

entries.name: The Break Room
entries.story: South Burlington's smash room announced it was closing for good, with a final week of bookings and a plea to use gift cards before the last day.

entries.name: Esox
entries.story: The chalk-graffiti-covered, Yankees-loving dive bar across from the courthouse posted its own headstone on social media — 'October 2, 1978 – August 15, 2026' — citing a rent dispute with Delta Properties. It opened as Atwater Kent before taking the name of the Northern pike's genus in the '80s.

entries.name: Homeport at the Essex Experience
entries.dateLabel: soft opened July · grand opening August 1, 2026
entries.story: The Church Street housewares mainstay opened a second, 6,000-square-foot store at the Essex Experience — kitchen goods and housewares, timed to the flagship's 20th anniversary.

entries.name: Kitchen Table (both locations)
entries.story: Both Kitchen Table spots — the restaurant in Richmond and the market on Williston Road — closed in early August, with Mirabelles Bakery taking over the pair.

entries.name: Artemus Café and Burlington Art Mini Museum
entries.story: The narrow former Cosmic Grind storefront is being reborn as a café-slash-mini-museum, pouring Brio coffee and selling local art on a sliding-scale commission.

entries.name: Black Ice Premium Ice Cream
entries.story: Three homeschooled teenage brothers — Malachi, Messiah and Jaleel McMillan — run this creemee stand their dad helped them build as a daily lesson in entrepreneurship, with açaí bowls and dye-free creemees on the menu.

entries.name: The Café HOT.
entries.story: Brothers Allan and Travis Walker-Hodkin are permanently closing the breakfast spot behind the Bon Appétit-noted #8 sandwich and returning to New York to be closer to family — staying open only until a new tenant takes the space.

entries.name: Vermont Comedy Arts theater
entries.story: Vermont Comedy Club's nonprofit arm is opening a 30-to-40-seat basement theater across the street from the club, in the space that belonged to the Drink bar — deliberately booze-free, built to give local standups, sketch and improv acts real stage time plus kids' programming.

entries.name: J.Jill
entries.story: The women's clothing retailer is under construction on Walnut Street at Maple Tree Place — the second national clothing brand to join the center this year, after J.Crew's spring opening.

entries.name: Wild Meadows Books & Café
entries.dateLabel: opened early July 2026 · grand opening July 11–12
entries.story: The Williston Observer's owners opened the town's only general-interest bookstore, with local art on the walls and Mirabelles treats at the café counter.

entries.name: The Harborvale
entries.story: The former Courtyard by Marriott reopened as a 161-room Autograph Collection hotel from the Hotel Vermont team, with chef Doug Paine's Lake Champlain-focused restaurant.

entries.name: Nostalgia Toys & More
entries.story: The retro toy shop lasted seven months in the corner storefront that was Weenies Hot Dogs — rent, staffing, and theft made it unsustainable, the owners said.

entries.name: Old Brick Store outpost (Public Service VT)
entries.area: Karma Bird House, Maple St, Burlington
entries.story: The team behind Charlotte's beloved Old Brick Store takes over the Kestrel Coffee café space at Karma Bird House — pastries, espresso, and prepared food, "the Brick on a small scale."

entries.name: Judi's Ice Cream (City Center)
entries.story: The local ice cream name is expanding to South Burlington's City Center, which keeps stacking up local food businesses.

entries.name: Feldman's Bagels
entries.story: The South End bagel shop went out of business overnight — customers found a handwritten sign on the door; the St. Albans location closed the same day.

entries.name: Burl's Downtown Kitchenette
entries.story: The Farmhouse Group turned the 1954 Oasis diner car into an all-day Southern-leaning diner — biscuits and gravy, fried chicken and waffles, patty melts, a full bar.

entries.name: El Cortijo Taqueria
entries.story: After 15 years the Farmhouse Group's taqueria served its last tacos in the Bank Street diner car, making way for Burl's Downtown Kitchenette.

entries.name: Lippa's Estate & Fine Jewelry
entries.story: A family business that opened in 1933 is decamping for an appointment-only showroom in Colchester after 93 years downtown — owner Michael Berger cited hiring troubles and a pivot toward wholesale.

entries.name: Offbeat Creemee
entries.story: After five years, Aisha and Danny Bassett closed the dairy-free creemee business that began at Winooski's Myers Memorial Pool in 2021 — ingredient costs had doubled, and they'd welcomed a daughter over the winter. They'd love to see someone carry the brand forward.

entries.name: El Gato Cantina (Essex Junction)
entries.area: Park St at Five Corners, Essex Junction
entries.story: After a dozen years at the Five Corners, the Mexican restaurant closed ahead of the building's planned demolition — it's hunting a new Essex-area home, and the Jeffersonville and Smugglers' Notch spots carry on.

entries.name: PopUp Bagels
entries.dateLabel: announced May 2026 · no opening date yet
entries.story: The fast-growing chain known for bagel-and-schmear combos with rotating specialty cream cheeses picked the Marketplace storefront Black Cap Coffee left behind for its first Vermont outpost.

entries.name: J.Crew
entries.story: The national clothing brand filled a former Mexican-restaurant space at Maple Tree Place — one of several big names landing in Williston's shopping hub this year.

entries.name: Earth Prime Comics + Quarterstaff Games
entries.story: The two longtime Church Street fixtures, founded by the late Christine Farrell in the 1980s, merged and reopened in the new Burlington Square development — fully accessible for the first time, with room to actually host Magic and Pokémon events.

entries.name: Dumpling Café
entries.story: Longtime Asiana House owner Gary Ma reopened 191 Pearl Street under a new concept focused on housemade dim sum — soup dumplings, steamed rice rolls with shrimp, crispy roasted pork belly — with a dim sum chef recruited from Boston.

entries.name: Chicken Charlie's Rotisserie, Grill & BBQ
entries.story: The 25-year-old restaurant closed while its ownership group evaluates the brand's future — it lost its seating when Kitchen Table Market & Café expanded into the space, and staffing challenges compounded the squeeze. No permanent decision has been made.

entries.name: Sabah's House
entries.story: Sabah Abbas and her son Mustafa Khudaier — a family who came to Vermont as refugees from the Iraq War — won a three-year lease on the 135-square-foot Marketplace kiosk, replacing Leunig's Petit Bijou with year-round shawarma, cardamom tea, pastries, and coffee.

entries.name: Thingz From Yaad Kitchen (downtown move)
entries.story: The popular Jamaican restaurant is leaving South Burlington for the former Sushi Maeda space downtown — three times larger, with a 20-plus-seat bar and a Caribbean cocktail menu where every drink gets a Jamaican patois name.

entries.name: Church Street cart vendors: Tambo, Bernique's Boutique, Watercolors by Joshy
entries.story: Three new Vermont-based cart vendors joined nine returning ones on the bricks: Tambo (Peruvian food), Bernique's Boutique (African crafts), and Watercolors by Joshy (wearable watercolor art).

entries.name: Small Dog Electronics (retail store)
entries.story: The region's only approved Apple repair-and-resell shop closed its Burlington storefront and moved the business online.

entries.name: Sweetwaters
entries.story: The Church Street staple is back at its original address after a four-year hiatus, with head chef Jessee Lawyer — who started there as a fry cook — reviving the cornflake-crusted chicken fingers and bringing back the smoker.

entries.name: Kestrel Coffee Roasters (Pine St)
entries.story: The Pine Street café poured its last shots mid-April — "all good things evolve," the owners said; their other locations stayed open.

entries.name: Alimentari Café & Provisions
entries.story: Pizzeria Verità co-owner Leslie McCrorey Wells filled the former Café St. Paul space with a daytime Italian café — housemade mozzarella, espresso, an all-day sandwich menu, and pantry goods from Italy and beyond.

entries.name: Whim Boutique
entries.story: The women's clothing shop that folded into the now-shuttered Dear Lucy is coming back under Ava Stanley, its manager from 2018 to 2021 — a vote of confidence for a Marketplace that has lost several fashion retailers.

entries.name: Café Napoli
entries.dateLabel: announced · was aiming for late March 2026 — opening unconfirmed
entries.story: After a decade pulling shots at the Cosmic Grind, barista Cole Thornton opened his own espresso bar with partner Dante Seguino in the cozy space that once housed Lucky Next Door.

entries.name: La Casa del Sabor
entries.story: The Arteaga-Pineda family opened an Ecuadorian restaurant in the spot where Pauline's Café ran for almost fifty years — cheese-stuffed potato pancakes plus Peruvian and Colombian dishes, a full bar, and weekend coastal seafood specials.

entries.name: Slide In Pub
entries.story: North London transplant Joseph Fox opened Vermont's first-ever soccer bar — 10 televisions with Switchback and Fiddlehead on tap, and a full house of singing England supporters by World Cup time.

entries.name: Savu Sauna bathhouse
entries.story: The outdoor-sauna company that's been steaming lakeside since 2021 is building an 8,000-square-foot bathhouse — multiple saunas, a steam room, warm pools, and a cold plunge.

entries.name: Pizzeria Corinna
entries.story: Shane Corbett's nostalgia-driven pizza shop channels the pizzerias of the late '80s — six pies, Italian subs named after Ninja Turtles on house-baked seeded semolina rolls, and 60 loaves a day from baker Olivia Clemons.

entries.name: Dear Lucy
entries.story: The longtime Church Street shoe store closed its doors, its owner saying retail — and downtown — had changed.

entries.name: Thai in the Alley
entries.story: The alley spot behind the Marketplace is back in business, replacing BKK in the Alley — the Stowe Thai Cuisine owner and chef Tokyo Asissara serve a menu that roams Thailand's regions.

entries.name: Mothership Brewery
entries.story: The brewpub at American Flatbread — the very room where Zero Gravity was born in 2004 — relaunched as Mothership Brewery under head brewer Destiny Saxon, taps pouring only at the Hearth.

entries.name: Drink
entries.area: St. Paul St at City Hall Park, Burlington
entries.story: The low-key cocktail bar across from City Hall Park — born in 1999 as Wine Works and rebranded a few times since — called it after more than a quarter century of trivia, comedy, and live music.

entries.name: Instant House
entries.story: UVM grad Bishnu Pokhrel opened a self-serve instant ramen bar in the South Korean style blowing up on TikTok — pick a packaged ramen, pile on toppings, and cook it yourself on induction burners, with milk teas and boba on the side.

entries.name: Mountain Valley Indian Cuisine
entries.story: The couple behind Winooski's Mountain Valley Restaurant brought their tandoori, curries, and hand-pleated momos to a former Domino's on Farrell Street.

entries.name: Pascolo Ristorante
entries.story: The Italian spot moved back into its original subterranean home at 83 Church Street after three years up the block — same menu, same staff.

entries.name: Peak Makaya Coffee Co-op
entries.story: Artist and nonprofit founder Pievy Polyte opened a retail store and gallery selling Haitian Blue Mountain coffee, cocoa, and his own paintings — proceeds support schools and medical services in his home region of Haiti.

entries.name: Black Cap Coffee & Bakery (Church St)
entries.story: Two years of sliding sales ended the Church Street café's run days after its baristas walked out; the non-union Stowe, Morrisville, and Waterbury shops carry on.

entries.name: Scale Poké Bar
entries.story: The poké chain's third Vermont location landed in South Burlington's City Center neighborhood.

entries.name: Partizanfilm
entries.story: A member-run nonprofit micro-cinema filled the void the Roxy left — two intimate screening rooms (31 and 19 seats) and a café-bookstore lobby, programmed seven days a week.

entries.name: Clover Café
entries.story: Siblings Amaya and Wolf Baustert aimed for a December launch with Brio Coffeeworks espresso and local pastries from Sweet Alchemy and Klinger's in a high-visibility spot with big, bright windows.

entries.name: The Chocolate Butcher Chop Shop
entries.story: Rough-cut chocolate chunks, truffles, and snack boards, sold butcher-style in Williston.

entries.name: Specs cocktail bar
entries.story: After a year of Friday pop-ups, Sam Nelis unveiled his long-awaited 10-seat bar with more than 100 classic cocktails, launched with a day of live music.

entries.name: Doma Bar
entries.story: The former Paradiso Hi-Fi space reopened as a cocktails-and-vinyl lounge pitched as "your coolest friend's living room" — the hi-fi system and hundreds of albums stayed, joined by a disco ball, fried cheese curds, and Puerto Rican-influenced cocktails.

entries.name: Citizen Cider Press House Pub
entries.story: After permitting delays pushed it months past target, the cidery consolidated under one roof on Flynn Avenue — indoor food-truck kitchen, smash burgers, and the full tap list.

entries.name: Charlotte Sailing Center
entries.story: Andy O'Brien's marina got the boot after 20 years when Lake Champlain Transportation declined to renew his lease, sending dozens of boat owners scrambling for new moorings.

entries.name: Asiana House
entries.story: The Pearl Street sushi spot went dark for seven months before owner Gary Ma announced he was done doing sushi after a lifetime of it — the space reopened as his Dumpling Café in May 2026.

entries.name: Mr. Creemee
entries.story: The Little Gordo team opened a sherbet-colored Pine Street parlor with housemade doughnuts and the ultimate doughnut ice cream sandwich.

entries.name: Simple Roots Brewing
entries.area: North Ave, New North End, Burlington
entries.story: After 11 years, owners Dan Ukolowicz and Kara Pawlusiak closed the New North End brewery — "the hardest part for us is closing an incredible community space where people have gathered for many years."

entries.name: Mandarin
entries.story: When his head chef retired and no qualified replacement could be found, Lawrence Fong closed the seven-year-old restaurant — ending nearly four decades of Fong family Chinese restaurants in Chittenden County, from the original Mandarin on Church Street to Joyce's Noodle House in Essex.

entries.name: Ridin' High
entries.story: Big John Van Hazinga's tiny hut at Battery and Pearl had been a colorful cornerstone of Burlington's skate scene since 2003 — it survived a near-fatal crash and a federal indictment, but not residential zoning violations. He hoped to relocate to Montgomery Center.

entries.name: BKK in the Alley
entries.story: The Thai spot tucked behind the Marketplace closed in the fall — the space came back to life as Thai in the Alley the following January.

entries.name: Burlington Square (AC Hotel by Marriott)
entries.story: A decade after the mall came down, "the Pit" became Burlington Square — a 161-room AC Hotel, 53 apartments, and street-level food, with a second tower still to come.

entries.name: La Di Da Pizza
entries.story: New York native Celine Eid turned the former Despacito space into a NYC-style slice shop, with seasonal pies and grab-and-go energy in the Old North End.

entries.name: T & M Asian Market
entries.story: Roasted duck and dim sum from Boston, fresh Asian vegetables, ramen, dumplings, and even Labubu dolls arrived in the growing neighborhood near Taft Corners' new hotels and housing.

entries.name: The Gryphon
entries.story: The Main Street gastropub closed after 11 years, citing a "trying last year" of construction detours and downtown struggles — weeks after Nectar's went dark up the street.

entries.name: Paradiso Hi-Fi
entries.story: The Pine Street listening bar went quiet, and by September plans were already in motion for Doma Bar to take over the space — keeping the sound system but relaxing the serious listening-lounge vibe.

entries.name: Riko's Pizza
entries.story: The Connecticut tavern-style pizza chain opened with fanfare in late January and was gone by mid-August — the franchisee said the location didn't fit the brand's growth plans.

entries.name: Gardener's Supply (Shelburne seasonal store)
entries.story: When Indiana-based Gardens Alive! bought the iconic Vermont company out of bankruptcy for $9 million, it kept five of six retail locations open — only the seasonal Shelburne store got the axe.

entries.name: Nectar's
entries.story: The club that gave Phish its start played its final set after nearly 50 years — construction, changing nightlife, and failed lease talks finally ended a Burlington institution.

entries.name: Playa Bowls
entries.story: The açaí-bowl chain's first Vermont location joined the Dorset Street food rush.

entries.name: Wings Over Burlington
entries.story: The wing shop returned to Dorset Street under corporate ownership, four months after the franchise abruptly closed.

entries.name: Le Bon GoûT
entries.story: More than two decades after arriving from Togo, Elom Essiba turned her catering business into a daily takeout spot at the Myers Memorial Pool concession stand — jollof rice, fufu, and authentic African dishes for the Onion City.

entries.name: Half Pint Pizza
entries.story: The Daily Planet team set up a permanent pizza kitchen inside their friends' brewery — a symbiotic South Burlington pairing that gives beer drinkers a reason to stay.

entries.name: Philo Ridge Farm (market & restaurant)
entries.story: The regenerative farm's market and restaurant reopened after being closed since late 2023 while the operation transitioned to a nonprofit — a big win for fans of its farm-to-table dining.

entries.name: Café St. Paul
entries.story: The St. Paul Street café closed in a spring that took several local spots with it — the space found a second life as Alimentari Café & Provisions the following April.

entries.name: Sushi Maeda
entries.story: The Cherry Street sushi restaurant closed; Thingz From Yaad Kitchen later announced it would take over the space for its downtown move.

entries.name: The Cup & Leaf
entries.story: The Essex tea spot closed in the same wave of spring 2025 restaurant and café exits reported across Chittenden County.

entries.name: The District VT (formerly ArtsRiot)
entries.dateLabel: closed late May 2025 · weeks after rebrand
entries.story: The Pine Street venue shut its doors "effective immediately" just weeks after shedding the ArtsRiot name, capping years of ownership churn — all upcoming shows canceled.

entries.name: Despacito
entries.story: The vegan, Puerto Rican-influenced restaurant announced its closure and offered its kitchen and lease for $40,000 — the North Winooski Avenue space later became La Di Da Pizza.

entries.name: Joann Fabrics
entries.story: The fabric and craft chain shut down all its regional stores as the national company wound down — a third closed in late April, the rest by the end of May.

entries.name: The Farmhouse Tap & Grill (Williston)
entries.story: Fifteen years after establishing itself as a Burlington go-to, the Farmhouse Group announced a second Farmhouse Tap & Grill for Williston, bringing its farm-to-table fare to Finney Crossing.

entries.name: PayMore
entries.story: The electronics buyback shop gives that drawer of tangled chargers and retro consoles a second life — recycling, but with cash back.

entries.name: The Mad Taco (Shelburne Rd)
entries.story: The Vermont taco mini-chain rolled its fifth location — a food truck parked at the new Gardener's Supply — so plant shopping and taco feasting now go hand in hand.

entries.name: Firehouse Subs
entries.story: The national sandwich chain's first-ever Vermont restaurant opened in Williston, with a slice of each sale going to public-safety groups.

entries.name: Manhattan's (Manhattan Pizza & Pub)
entries.story: The late-night pizza-and-music corner was shut by the fire marshal over unpermitted work weeks after reopening as Manhattan's — it never came back, and What Ales You later claimed the space.
